newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - July 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - July 1.

text.p: Following are the highlights of Irish press on Tuesday:

- Former prime minister Charles Haughey is to give evidence to the Dunnes tribunal as to how he received 1.3 million Irish pounds from Ben Dunne "as a matter of probability" but did not know who the donor was at the time.
- Minister for the Marine Michael Woods had demanded full information from the UK authorities about the secret dumping of radioactive material in the Irish Sea 30 to 40 years ago.

- Drumcree and the British-Irish compromise proposals on decommissioning are expected to be top of the agenda when Ireland's newly-elected prime minister Bertie Ahern meets Northern Ireland Secretary Mo Mowlam in Belfast today.
- A consortium in which Irish airports authority Aer Rianta has a substantial interest has been shortlisted to buy a 50 percent stake in Duesseldorf Airport, Germany's second largest.
- Charles Haughey was probably given the 1.3 million punts at the centre of the Dunnes payments tribunal, his lawyer said.
- A murder investigation was underway last night after the death of a man who was attacked in Dundalk.

- Mary O'Rourke, the new Minister for Public Enterprise, has turned down a request from Esat Telecom to abolish the EU derogation which protects Telecom Eireann from full competition for residential phone traffic until January 1, 2000.
- Special new courses to fill the growing skills shortage in industry are expected to cost between 16 and 20 million.
- Charles Haughey yesterday conceded the 1.3 million at the centre of the payments to politicians tribunal was paid into bank accounts for his benefit.
- Property prices in one of Ireland's most popular tourist areas, Dingle, are going through the roof amid reports that two well-known premises have fetched almost 1.5 million between them.

- Avonmore and Waterford Foods are confident that the ballot next week on their proposed 2.5 billion merger will secure the required 75 percent majority following the successful conclusion of the shareholder information meetings.
